model.label: Social health insurance with a single public payer, the National Health Fund (NFZ), funded mainly by a 9% earmarked health contribution plus state-budget subsidies; publicly and privately owned providers under NFZ contracts; high out-of-pocket spending on outpatient medicines

overview.statement: Poland's health system is built on social health insurance that covers roughly 97% of the population; most people without cover are registered as residents but live outside the country.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

overview.statement: Governance, financing and purchasing sit mainly with the Ministry of Health and the National Health Fund (NFZ); the 16 regions own the larger regional hospitals and the 314 counties own the smaller county hospitals.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

overview.statement: Most primary care practices and most specialist outpatient providers are privately owned, and any private provider may treat patients either free of charge under an NFZ contract or for a private fee.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

overview.statement: Regional NFZ branches buy care in their territories under contracts open to public and private providers, but the package of guaranteed services is fixed centrally, so purchasing can be adapted to local needs only a little.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

overview.statement: Under the Act on health care services financed from public funds, people covered by universal compulsory or voluntary health insurance have a legal right to publicly financed care, as do some uninsured residents, including Polish citizens living in Poland who meet the income criterion of the social assistance act.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

overview.statement: In 2023, 96.9% of Poland's population was formally enrolled in social health insurance, and pregnant women and children under 18 are entitled to publicly funded care regardless of whether they are insured.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

overview.statement: Uninsured people outside the protected groups can still use outpatient emergency care and primary care without paying at the time, but they may be billed afterwards.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: Public sources paid for 77.8% of health spending in 2023, a share that has risen steadily; social health insurance contributions, collected mainly as earmarked payroll taxes, are the core of public funding.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: Health insurance contributions, mostly an earmarked payroll tax, supply about 90% of publicly financed current health spending; money from general taxation in the state budget pays for public health programmes, among other things.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: The health insurance contribution is set by law at 9% of the contribution base, subject to exceptions in other articles of the Act.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: For employees, the law makes the employer the payer that calculates the health contribution, takes it out of the insured worker's income and remits it, so the contribution is withheld from pay.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: Self-employed people taxed under article 30c of the personal income tax act pay a health contribution of 4.9% of their contribution base; where the contribution is calculated monthly, it may not be less than 9% of the minimum wage in force on the first day of the contribution year.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: A tax reform raised the health contributions paid by higher-income self-employed people, which increased the NFZ's revenue.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: The law sets a floor for public health funding of 7% of GDP a year, with lower interim minimums through 2026, including 6.5% of GDP in 2025 and 6.8% in 2026.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: When the government pledged in 2018 to raise public health spending as a share of GDP, it redefined how that share is calculated, so national figures differ markedly from those of international sources.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: In a release dated 23 October 2026, the NFZ said the state budget subsidy for 2026 then stood at almost PLN 37 billion, and that its funds for patient care in 2026 totalled PLN 227.37 billion, over PLN 13 billion more than in the original financial plan.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: Since 2022 the NFZ has also paid for some services for population groups exempt from paying contributions, and since 2023 it has carried the full cost of emergency care.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: Out-of-pocket payments by households were the second-largest funding source, at 15.7% of current health spending in 2023, slightly above the EU average of 15.5%.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financing.statement: Voluntary health insurance, which supplements and complements the statutory system, accounted for 6.5% of health spending in 2023.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

covered.statement: The law lists the guaranteed benefit areas, including primary care, specialist outpatient care, care in county health centres, hospital treatment, psychiatric and addiction care, medical rehabilitation, long-term nursing and care, dental treatment, spa treatment, prescribed medical devices and emergency medical services.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

covered.statement: Hospital care is covered broadly: public financing pays 95% of inpatient care costs, against an EU average of 91%, so there is virtually no cost-sharing for inpatient care.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

covered.statement: Public coverage is narrow for dental care, outpatient medicines, therapeutic appliances and rehabilitation; covered dental care is limited to essential services with volume and frequency limits, such as dentures only once every five years.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

covered.statement: Covered rehabilitation is limited to outpatient settings and to at most 40 days a year for a given problem.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

covered.statement: Cancer drugs are paid for through a positive list, high-cost medicines through drug programmes for defined patient groups with strict criteria, and a separate Medical Fund pays for high-cost innovative therapies; all medicines prescribed and given in hospital are free to patients.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

covered.statement: Primary care is free at the point of use, but public funds covered only 36% of the cost of pharmaceuticals and medical non-durables.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

covered.statement: Public provision of long-term care is limited and the sector relies heavily on informal carers.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

covered.statement: New therapies funded through the Medical Funds and placed on the cancer drugs list are selected through a process that uses health technology assessment, especially cost-effectiveness analysis, to inform both coverage and the price negotiations run by the Ministry of Health's Economic Commission.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

covered.statement: For new medicines or new indications to be publicly reimbursed, a cost-effectiveness threshold has been applied since 2012, but it is only one of 13 criteria in pricing and reimbursement decisions and is not obligatory.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

covered.statement: Of the medicines given EU marketing authorisation from 2020 to 2023, 40% are available in Poland to various patient groups, with health technology assessment used to restrict coverage to the patients most likely to benefit.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: Within the public system, primary care, specialist outpatient care and hospital care, including medicines used in hospital, are free of charge.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: From 1 September 2023, free prescription medicines were extended from pregnant women and people aged 75 and over to children under 18 and people aged 65 and over; military veterans and blood or organ donors also qualify.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: There is no exemption from medicine co-payments for people on low incomes and no overall ceiling on co-payments.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: For medicines taken for up to 30 days, patients pay 30% or 50% of the price, and in addition whatever the retail price exceeds the reference price by; for longer courses or costlier drugs they pay a flat EUR 0.71 for each pack (up to 30 defined daily doses) plus the same excess.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: In 2023 statutory funds paid for only about a third of retail pharmaceutical spending, and patients paid almost two thirds directly.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: No cost-sharing applies to covered dental care, but many dental services are outside the benefits package and are bought privately.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financial_hardship.statement: Out-of-pocket payments for medicines are the main driver of catastrophic household health spending in Poland, though their share of catastrophic payments fell from 57% in 2013 to 44% in 2021.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financial_hardship.statement: Households in the poorest consumption quintile are the most likely to incur catastrophic health payments; the odds are about 80% lower for the second quintile and about 90% lower for the third to fifth.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financial_hardship.statement: The odds of catastrophic health spending are higher for rural than urban households (by 15%), for households with three or more children than for childless ones (by 45%), and for households of retirees, pensioners and farmers than for employees' households.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

financial_hardship.statement: Pensioners, disabled people and rural households continue to spend especially heavily on outpatient medicines, even after co-payment exemptions were introduced for older people (2016) and pregnant women (2020).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

additional_care.statement: Voluntary health insurance has a growing role as supplementary and complementary cover.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

additional_care.statement: Public hospitals may provide private care only if they operate as commercial-code companies, which account for about 15% of all hospital beds.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

additional_care.statement: Difficulty getting outpatient services may push people who can afford it toward private providers.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

additional_care.statement: In a nationwide online survey of 1,162 adults in August 2025, 82.9% said the private sector does better on waiting times, 60.1% on staff courtesy and 58.5% on booking and cancelling appointments.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

additional_care.statement: Half of the respondents (50.5%) rated the competence of medical staff as equally good in public and private services, and none of the eight aspects asked about was rated better in public services.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

access.statement: In 2024, 5.2% of people in Poland who needed medical care reported that they could not get it because of cost, waiting times or travel distance, above the EU average of 3.6% for 2023.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

access.statement: Waiting times mainly affect specialist outpatient services, some specialist elective inpatient care and rehabilitation, and have been particularly long in some highly specialised fields such as endocrinology.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

access.statement: Average waits in 2024 were 156 days for a hip replacement, down from 298 days in 2019, and 231 days for a knee replacement, down from 403 days.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

access.statement: The NFZ began lifting annual volume caps for outpatient providers in 2015 and removed all of them in 2021, but without the funds to pay for all services delivered, so many providers ran budget deficits.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

access.statement: In 2023 Poland had 3.9 practising physicians per 1,000 people against an EU average of 4.3, and 5.9 nurses per 1,000 against 8.5.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

access.statement: General practitioners made up 6.7% of physicians in 2023, one of the lowest shares in the EU (average 19.9%); internists and paediatricians also still provide primary care.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

access.statement: Primary care is easy to reach: patients can usually be seen the same day in smaller private GP practices (though large public facilities may have long waits), practices are open about 50 hours a week, and care is available out of hours, at weekends and on public holidays.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

access.statement: People in rural areas have worse access to specialist care than people in cities.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

access.statement: Waits stem from severe health workforce shortages and NFZ budget limits on the volume of contracted services, and Poland has no waiting-time guarantees.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

access.statement: Primary care doctors usually act as gatekeepers to specialists, but no referral is required for gynaecologists, obstetricians, oncologists, psychiatrists or dentists.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

outcomes.statement: Life expectancy at birth dropped by 2.6 years between 2019 and 2021, then reached a record 78.7 years in 2024.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

outcomes.statement: Preventable mortality was 244 deaths per 100,000 people in 2022, compared with 168 across the EU.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

outcomes.statement: Mortality from treatable causes was 140 per 100,000 in 2022, against an EU average of 90.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

outcomes.statement: Avoidable hospital admissions for asthma and COPD were relatively low in 2023, but avoidable admissions for congestive heart failure were high.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

locator.table: Table (unnumbered): HAQ Index estimates, by location, in 2019 and absolute change from 1990 to 2019; 2019 HAQ Index columns in order: overall 0-74, young 0-14, working 15-64, post-working 65-74 years

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

outcomes.statement: In-hospital death rates after admission for heart attack are relatively low, though they could fall further.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

costs.statement: In 2023 health spending equalled 7.2% of GDP, far below the EU average of 10%.

costs.statement: Inpatient services took 37.2% of current health spending in 2023 (EU average 27.7%) and outpatient services 30.5% (EU average 27.6%).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

costs.statement: In 2023 only 7.8% of current health spending went to long-term care, under half the EU average of 18.1%, and 1.7% went to prevention, against 4% in the EU.

costs.statement: Health took 12.2% of total government spending in 2023, below the EU average of 14.8%, but that share has been rising faster in Poland than in the EU.

costs.statement: Per person, Poland spent EUR 352 on retail pharmaceuticals in 2023, about a third less than the EU average of EUR 510 (purchasing-power adjusted).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents, two rounds)

costs.statement: Hospital bed numbers remain relatively high and occupancy low by EU standards, which points to excess hospital capacity.

what_works.statement: Waiting times fell because the system was funded to pay for the larger volume of care that was needed.

changelog.note: Profile created: 99 claims from 11 sources, anchored and support-reviewed in a separate cold pass by independent reviewer agents (two rounds). Round 1 failed 35 statements: 34 fixed (rewording, re-anchoring to wider passages that name their subject or year, or removing details not in the passage) and 1 dropped (POL-financing-005); round 2 failed 3 more (missing or unsupported years), fixed. 2 statements reworded earlier to remove copied wording.
